title: Introduce RAG local-prover playground for e2e authoring and telemetry probes
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: customers asked for a compact, reproducible quickstart that demonstrates end-to-end RAG authoring with stepwise verification and lightweight telemetry probes that run locally (no hosted account required). This PR adds a standalone quickstart called 'rag-local-prover' that bundles an incremental indexer, a tiny local retriever, an authoring REPL, an example agent that performs tool-calling, and a small test harness for smoke e2e flows. Goals: 1) give developers a sandbox to iterate on prompts, retrieval configs, and structured output assertions; 2) show how to attach telemetry probes and breakpoints to validate hallucination regressions during authoring; 3) provide cross-language examples (TypeScript and Python) and a CI smoke job that runs the quickstart in a headless mode. What changed (high level): added quickstarts/rag-local-prover with README, step-by-step authoring guide, two example agents (TS/PY), an incremental indexing helper script, a telemetry probe shim, and a GitHub Actions workflow for quickstart smoke tests. Includes minimal Dockerfile for the local runner and a devcontainer for fast onboarding. Checklist: - [x] quickstart content and examples - [x] CI smoke workflow - [x] README with troubleshooting - [x] telemetry probe examples and explanation - [x] basic unit/e2e tests - [x] docs cross-link to docs site (docs PR queued separately) Usage summary: run ./dev.sh to build a local sandbox that spins up a memory-based retriever and a stub LLM server (open-source wasm shim included), then run the authoring REPL to iterate. The telemetry probes emit JSON traces to ./telemetry/out which the README documents how to inspect. Related Linear: ENG-4321 (authoring UX), PM-120 (quickstart outreach). Related Jira: SUP-991 (customer request). Notes: this quickstart purposefully keeps the model stub minimal (deterministic token sequences) so CI is deterministic and the telemetry assertions are reliable. The docs cross-link will be submitted in a follow-up docs PR to update the central quickstarts index. Merge rationale: low risk, developer-facing content behind a new path that does not change runtime code.
